newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan not offended by lack of mention by Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Japan not offended by lack of mention by Clinton.

text.p: Japan, which accounts for the largest part of the U.S. trade deficit, said on Wednesday it was not offended that it failed to event rate a mention in President Bill Clinton's State of the Union address to Congress.

"Although Japan was not mentioned in his speech, both President Clinton and we have said on various occasions that Japan and the United States are pillars of various relations," top government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference.
"Previously, President Clinton mentioned the importance of Japan-U.S. relations. We feel that President Clinton broadened his scope this time to mention Asia as a whole," Kajiyama said.
On U.S. foreign policy in Asia, President Clinton mentioned China, South Korea and North Korea.
"Japan will continue to cooperate with President Clinton in his second term to ensure peace and stability in the Asia-Pacific region as well as the rest of the world," Kajiyama said.
